newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda opposes Zaire role for those "tainted in Africa".
newsitem.headline: Uganda opposes Zaire role for those "tainted in Africa".

text.p: Uganda said on Wednesday it was opposed to involvement in eastern Zaire by countries who had been "tainted in Africa" such as France and Britain.

At a news conference, Minister of State for International Cooperation Martin Aliker said Kampala would only fully support an international intervention force to guarantee humanitarian work among refugees in Zaire if it was neutral.
"We are in favour of a 'neutral' international force. The the operational word is neutral. For example, we would support say the Swedes, the Canadians, the Australians," he said.
Asked if Uganda opposed a role by France and Britain, Aliker said: "We do not support anybody who has had their names tainted in Africa."

Canada said it was ready to lead the multinational force in Zaire. France, Spain, Mali and South Africa have pledged troops to a force to help hundreds of thousands of mainly ethnic Hutu refugees at risk of dying.
Britain, France, Belgium and Portugal were leading colonial powers in Africa.
